topic.readerProblem: A marketer or founder wants to know whether ChatGPT leans on Wikipedia and whether their brand should try to get a Wikipedia page to be cited or recommended.
topic.connection: Ties AI citation behaviour to the entity and earned-coverage signals AEOeye's audits look at, and points readers to what they can control: definition-first pages, sourced claims, consistent entity data and independent mentions.

assessment: The page answers yes with the one open study we could verify line by line (a 2025 University of Toronto preprint: about 19.7% of ChatGPT citations in a 50-prompt cola experiment, Wikipedia among its top domains in car queries), says OpenAI publishes no share, and explains the pull with documented facts (Wikimedia on LLM training, the GPT-3 data mix, Wikipedia's lead-section and verifiability rules). It then gives a clear position on whether brands should seek a page, based on WP:NCORP, WP:COI and the Wikimedia paid-contribution rule, and on what to do instead, using AEOeye's crawler access study for the Wikipedia/Reddit robots.txt contrast and schema sameAs prevalence. It deliberately does not quote vendor citation-share studies whose methods could not be checked, and does not claim a Wikipedia page improves AI recommendations.

sources.supports: Chen et al. (Sept 2025): AI search leans on earned media; in the 50-prompt cola experiment ChatGPT (OpenAI model with web search) cited Wikipedia for about 19.7% of citations; in electric-car, family-SUV and hybrid queries ChatGPT's top domains included Wikipedia, AP News and Reuters (all confirmed in the PDF text).
GPT-3 paper Table 2.2: Wikipedia 3 billion tokens, 3% weight in the training mix, 3.4 epochs (highest of the five datasets); 0.6% share of tokens is our own arithmetic (3 / 499 billion).

Wikimedia: almost all LLMs train on Wikipedia datasets; human pageviews down roughly 8% vs the same months of 2024, attributed to generative AI and social media, with search engines answering directly, often based on Wikipedia content (confirmed in raw HTML).

WP:NCORP: significant coverage in reliable, independent secondary sources; each source must be significant, independent, reliable and secondary and there must be multiple; press releases and sponsored articles do not count ('Only unpaid sources count'); a collection of trivial sources does not become significant; all content must be verifiable (confirmed in raw HTML).

WP:COI: COI editors strongly discouraged from editing affected articles directly; should disclose; propose changes on talk pages with the edit COI template; put new articles through Articles for Creation (confirmed in raw HTML).
Paid contributions must disclose each employer, client, intended beneficiary and affiliation on a user page, the talk page or in the edit summary (confirmed in raw HTML).

An item is acceptable if it has a valid sitelink, or refers to a clearly identifiable entity describable with serious and publicly available references, or fulfils a structural need (confirmed in raw HTML).

The lead should stand on its own as a concise overview: identify the topic, establish context, explain why it is notable, summarize the most important points including prominent controversies (confirmed in raw HTML).
sameAs is the URL of a reference web page that unambiguously indicates the item's identity, e.g. its Wikipedia page, Wikidata entry or official website (confirmed in raw HTML).
Definition link for Wikidata (page exists, HTTP 200).
